_README: Frozen requested -> canonical model id mapping, established by a live probe
of every condition on 2026-09-09 BEFORE the confirmatory grid.
PUBLIC ARTIFACT NOTE: the confirmatory runs were executed through a managed
execution path whose catalog used routing-specific request ids. Those ids
have been replaced throughout this public artifact by the corresponding
public model ids, so the OpenAI condition's requested id now equals its
canonical id. The substitution is 1:1 and changes no measurement: every
analysis keys off the canonical id, which is unchanged. The Bedrock
conditions gain a 'us.' region prefix and ':0' version separator upstream,
which is public provider behaviour and is preserved as observed.
Without this mapping the protocol's 'flag any canonical mismatch' rule would
flag every one of the 20,160 calls, which would make the check useless.
A call is FLAGGED when its returned model id is not the expected canonical
for the requested condition. Flagged runs are recorded and reported, never
probe_method: one live call per condition through the transport helper; canonical id read from the response 'model' field

notes.gpt-4o-2024-11-20: Requested and canonical ids are identical in this public artifact; the served snapshot is the public dated one.
notes.gemini-2.5-pro: Returns the alias unchanged - the managed execution path did NOT resolve it to a dated snapshot. Confirms the pinning limitation already disclosed: served weights may change during or between runs and this study cannot detect that from the id alone.
